sections.title: Evidential Faith and Worldview Comparison
sections.rationale: This section covers the dispute over whether biblical faith is evidence-grounded trust and which comparative standards can rationally distinguish Christian belief from skepticism or competing worldviews.

sections.title: Resurrection Evidence and Explanatory Inference
sections.rationale: This section covers the cumulative historical case for resurrection and the challenges from contested testimony, ordinary experience, martyr traditions, and rival explanations.

sections.title: Divine Hiddenness, Salvation, and Religious Experience
sections.rationale: This section joins the disputes over divine disclosure, freely formed relationship, hell, postmortem opportunity, present commitment, and naturalistic accounts of religious experience.

sections.title: Scriptural Transmission, Composition, and Reliability
sections.rationale: This section covers whether variants, disputes, discrepancies, multiple authorship, literary reuse, and culturally situated transmission remain compatible with historically and theologically usable Scripture.

sections.title: Exodus History and Ancient Interpretation
sections.rationale: This section covers the historical status of a minimal Exodus, archaeological ambiguity, demographic objections, ancient numerical conventions, and the accessibility of culturally distant revelation.

sections.title: Religious Diversity and Ancient Parallels
sections.rationale: This section covers the burden of privileging Christianity amid rival traditions and assesses whether miracle, exaltation, resurrection, and literary parallels undermine or preserve Christian distinctiveness.
